# Fixtures

A fixture is named by the case it covers, the mode, the build, the shape it holds, never by the
program it was captured from. The programs this tree runs are labelled by what they are:
`dos-real16` (real mode, a Borland map with publics), `dos-real16-alt` (a second real-mode
program, whose map has no publics) and `dos-djgpp32` (a DJGPP program under a DPMI host, paged).
A DOS file name inside a capture keeps its 8.3 length, so a neutral name stands in for it at the
same width.

A directory's PROVENANCE, where it has one, says how its files were captured.
